label: Appearance
value: Anne has a pointed freckled face.
unit: Anne is a skinny girl with a pointed freckled face, a little pointed chin, and solemn, big gray eyes. She has red hair that she wears in long braids, which Streams behind her in a bright torrent when unbraided, though some consider it auburn or Titian. At various points, her hair is dyed green, closely shingled, and eventually grows back into short, silky curls. She has ungracefully long, thin legs, stands taller than Miss Barry, and displays a pale style with cheeks that flush faintly pink.

label: Personality
value: Anne Shirley possesses a vivid imagination.
unit: A passionate and ambitious individual, she possesses a vivid imagination that frequently draws her into daydreams, though she is also described as heedless, impulsive, smart, and obedient. She holds strong aspirations, striving to become a teacher, emulate Mrs. Allan, and attend Redmond College while actively pursuing the Avery scholarship through hard work. Her academic efforts are further driven by a desire to make Matthew proud and a strong determination not to fail in front of Gilbert Blythe. Outside of her studies, she possesses a talent for storytelling and a praised singing voice. Her primary fears include going through the Haunted Wood after dark.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early years as an orphan living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and at an asylum before being brought to Green Gables. Though brought there by mistake instead of a boy, she was permitted to stay on probation with Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. Her volatile temper led to a clash with Mrs. Rachel Lynde over insults about her red hair, but Matthew persuaded her to apologize. After making a deep lifelong vow of friendship with Diana Barry, Anne faced a series of mishaps, including accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine and accidentally flavoring a cake for the new minister's wife with liniment. She also developed a bitter rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he teased her by calling her 'Carrots' and she broke a slate over his head. At school, Anne fell off a roof on a dare and broke her ankle, and she later dyed her hair green by mistake, forcing Marilla to cut it off. During a dramatic boat reenactment, she had to be rescued from a bridge pile by Gilbert, yet she maintained her refusal of his friendship. Anne joined Miss Stacy's advanced class to prepare for the Queen's Entrance examination, eventually tying for first place across the entire Island and earning a place at Queen's Academy. While attending Queen's, she won the prestigious Avery scholarship, but her life changed drastically when Matthew died suddenly following a bank failure.

After making a deep lifelong vow of friendship with Diana Barry, Anne faced a series of mishaps, including accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine and accidentally flavoring a cake for the new minister's wife with liniment. She also developed a bitter rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he teased her by calling her 'Carrots' and she broke a slate over his head. At school, Anne fell off a roof on a dare and broke her ankle, and she later dyed her hair green by mistake, forcing Marilla to cut it off. During a dramatic boat reenactment, she had to be rescued from a bridge pile by Gilbert, yet she maintained her refusal of his friendship. Anne joined Miss Stacy's advanced class to prepare for the Queen's Entrance examination, eventually tying for first place across the entire Island and earning a place at Queen's Academy. While attending Queen's, she won the prestigious Avery scholarship, but her life changed drastically when Matthew died suddenly following a bank failure.

value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."

label: Quote

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster.
unit: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster who boarded with her family at the time of her birth. When Anne Shirley moved to Green Gables, she and Diana met at Orchard Slope and instantly pledged to be lifelong bosom friends. Their friendship faced a brief separation when Diana's mother forbade her from playing with Anne, forcing the two girls to secretly exchange notes at school. However, after Anne successfully saved Diana's sick sister Minnie May from severe croup, Mrs. Barry lifted the ban and allowed their friendship to resume. Over the years, Diana remained a constant support to Anne, forming a story club with her, bringing her the exciting news that she tied for first place on the Queen's Entrance examination, and helping her dress for a high-profile benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel.

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it’s so black. He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers."

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta.
unit: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta caring for his sick father and a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick before returning to school. Upon his return, he teased Anne Shirley by calling her 'Carrots,' which resulted in Anne smashing her slate over his head and refusing his apology. This sparked an intense academic rivalry between the two students, though Gilbert rescued Anne when her boat began to leak and offered his friendship, which she angrily rejected. Their fierce competition continued through their time in the Queen's Entrance class and later at Queen's Academy, where Gilbert won the academic medal while Anne won the Avery Scholarship. Upon learning that Anne intended to stay at Green Gables after Matthew's death and Marilla's failing eyesight, Gilbert selflessly gave up his position as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne could take the post close to home, leading them to finally reconcile their long-standing feud and become close friends.

label: History
value: Josephine Barry visited Avonlea.
unit: Josephine Barry, an aunt from Charlottetown, visited Avonlea and was startled when Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally leaped onto her in bed. Though initially furious and threatening to cut off Diana's music lessons over the incident, she was amused and charmed by Anne's honest confession. Following their reconciliation, she forgave Diana, extended her stay in Avonlea, and formed a close friendship with Anne, later inviting her to visit her in the city.

label: Personality
value: Marilla is practical.
unit: A practical, sensible, and self-contained woman, Marilla possesses a rigid conscience and narrow experience, firmly disbelieving in imagining things to be different from reality. Characterized by an unsympathetic nature, she is strict and critical, being particularly fond of tacking a moral onto every remark made to a child. In line with her principles, she consistently refuses to criticize ministers, though she is inclined to become sarcastic when recovering from headaches. Despite being inexorable when setting disciplinary lessons, she has notably mellowed over time. She views it as her duty to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, and she is locally celebrated for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert went to collect an orphan boy to help on their farm.
unit: When Matthew Cuthbert went to collect an orphan boy to help on their farm, Marilla Cuthbert explained the plan to her neighbor Mrs. Rachel Lynde, but was shocked when Matthew instead brought home a girl named Anne. Though Marilla initially insisted on sending Anne back, she changed her mind after learning about Anne's tragic childhood and deciding not to hand her over to a harsh local woman. Taking responsibility for Anne's upbringing, Marilla began instructing her in neatness and religion, but was soon forced to send Anne to her room after the girl flew into a rage over Rachel's blunt insults. After Anne apologized and was permitted to stay, Marilla gradually developed a deep, warm affection for her, though she continued to strictly manage her. Marilla made plain clothes for Anne, scolded her for decorating her hat with wild flowers for church, and sent her into a dark spruce grove to cure her of dramatic fears about ghosts. Over the following years, Marilla supported Anne's growth, allowing her to attend a Sunday school picnic after realizing she had wrongly accused Anne of losing a missing brooch, and agreeing to let Anne join an advanced class to prepare for Queen's Academy. During Anne's broken ankle recovery, Marilla came to recognize how deeply she cared for the girl. When Matthew died suddenly following news of a bank failure, Marilla wept alongside Anne and opened up about a past youthful romance with John Blythe. Soon after, an oculist warned Marilla that she faced total blindness unless she gave up heavy eye work, leading Anne to forfeit her scholarship to remain at Green Gables and care for her.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert was an extremely shy man.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert was an extremely shy man who lived at Green Gables and spent decades wearing a full soft brown beard, avoiding almost all women except his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Due to his intense shyness, he rarely left his home, but he eventually traveled to Bright River station expecting to pick up an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on the farm. Instead, he discovered a young girl named Anne, and finding himself surprisingly fond of her talkative nature during the ride, he gently urged Marilla that they keep her. Over time, Matthew consistently supported Anne, bringing her sweeties, secretly encouraging her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde after a quarrel, and convincing Marilla to allow her to attend a local concert. Seeing that Anne lacked fashionable clothing, he overcame his deep shyness with female shopkeepers by arranging for Mrs. Lynde to sew Anne a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. Matthew offered warm encouragement for her schooling, felt immense pride when she tied for first place on the Island's Entrance examinations, and celebrated her commencement when she won the Avery Scholarship. Following a tender evening walk with Anne after her return home, Matthew collapsed and died suddenly from the shock of reading about a bank failure.

In her community, she is known as an active church worker who enjoys sewing, and she holds strong views as a passionate politician who remains firmly opposed to higher education for women.

value: Ruby Gillis is cheerful

She is deeply preoccupied with young men, aiming to have a beau by age fifteen, attract many suitors as she grows up, and marry after a brief two years of teaching. Additionally, she harbors a intense dread of caterpillars.

value: Anne and Diana walk to school.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: Anne and Diana walk to school, discussing the local students and Gilbert Blythe's return. During afternoon classes, Gilbert teases Anne by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' prompting Anne to smash her slate over his head. Mr. Phillips punishes Anne by making her stand at the blackboard, and she refuses to accept Gilbert's apology after school.

value: While Marilla is away in town, Diana seeks help at Green Gables.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla is away in town, Diana seeks help at Green Gables when her little sister Minnie May falls ill with severe croup. The next day, Mrs. Barry forgives Anne and invites her to resume her friendship with Diana.

Unmoved, Marilla forces Anne to walk through the woods as a lesson, curing Anne's desire for haunted places.

unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up heavy eye work or face total blindness, putting the future of Green Gables in jeopardy. After learning Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it, Anne meets Gilbert on her way home and they finally end their feud to become close friends.

unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

Marilla consults Rachel Lynde, who advises letting Anne cool off at home for a while. Later, Marilla is overcome with laughter when she finds Anne weeping over an imagined future scenario where Diana gets married and leaves her.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
value: Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend the concert.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend the concert and stay overnight at Diana's house, Anne and Diana enjoy the performance and return to Orchard Slope late at night. They run and leap onto the spare-room bed, inadvertently jumping on Diana's sleeping Great-Aunt Josephine. The next day, after learning that Miss Barry is furious and threatening to cut off Diana's music lessons, Anne expresses her remorse to Mrs. Lynde.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: After Mr. Phillips publicly punishes Anne for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe, she refuses to ever return to his school. Marilla consults Rachel Lynde, who advises letting Anne cool off at home for a while. Later, Marilla is overcome with laughter when she finds Anne weeping over an imagined future scenario where Diana gets married and leaves her.

value: Marilla returns home to Green Gables.
chapter: CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. When Marilla goes upstairs, she discovers Anne hiding under her pillows because she dyed her red hair green using hair dye bought from a peddler. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.
